title: Compound interest and savings
purpose: Two modes: grow a lump sum at a compound rate, or grow a monthly savings plan. Returns the future value, what you actually paid in, and how much of the total is growth.
formula:
Lump sum:
  FV = P (1 + r/100n)^(nt)
Monthly deposits, i = r/1200, m = 12t:
  FV = D ((1+i)^m - 1) / i
  at r = 0:  FV = D * m
prompts: Mode: 1 for a lump sum, 2 for monthly deposits
Mode 1: Principal, Rate % per year, Times/yr compounded (12 = monthly), Years
Mode 2: Monthly deposit, Rate % per year, Years (always compounded monthly)
test_case:
COMPOUND INTEREST
1 lump sum
2 monthly deposits
Mode: [1]
Principal: [1000]
Rate % /yr: [5]
Times/yr: [12]
Years: [10]
FV    = 1647.01
Grown = 647.01
quirks: Enter the rate as a PERCENT: type 5 for 5%, not 0.05.
Times/yr is the compounding frequency: 1 = annually, 4 = quarterly, 12 = monthly, 365 = daily.
A zero rate works in both modes. Mode 2 handles it as a special case because the annuity formula would divide by zero.
Zero years returns the principal unchanged, which is correct.
No currency symbol is printed - the euro sign is non-ASCII and renders badly on the calculator. The numbers are unitless, so use them for any currency.
Negative amounts are rejected. Times/yr must be greater than 0.
mode_note: Mode does not matter. COMPINT only does arithmetic and exponentiation, so the DEGREE / RADIAN setting has no effect on it.
